# a11y.aria-references — ARIA attribute points at an id that does not exist

- **Check ID:** `a11y.aria-references`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 1.3.1, WCAG 4.1.2
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.aria-references.md`](../a11y.aria-references.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

An ARIA attribute such as `aria-labelledby` lists an id that is not on the page.

## Why it matters

`aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, and the other reference attributes tell assistive technology to take a name or description from another element. When the id does not exist, the reference silently does nothing: a dialog has no name, a form field has no hint, a button controls nothing. Typical causes are a renamed id, an element that moved to another page, and ids generated at random in the markup but not in the label.

## What it checks

These attributes, with each space-separated id looked up among the ids on the same page: `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-owns`, `aria-flowto`, `aria-details`, `aria-activedescendant`, and `aria-errormessage`. A reference is reported when any id in the list is missing. Empty values are ignored. A legacy `<a name>` counts as an id, as it does for links.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before: there is no element with id="dialog-title" -->
<div role="dialog" aria-labelledby="dialog-title">
  <h2 id="title">Delete file</h2>
</div>

<!-- after -->
<div role="dialog" aria-labelledby="title">
  <h2 id="title">Delete file</h2>
</div>
```

If the name is plain text, `aria-label="Delete file"` is simpler and cannot break. There is no automatic edit, because the report cannot know which id was meant.

## Options

None.
